title: KV cache shadow-entry amplification after region failover — remediation and safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for the incident where a region failover coincident with aggressive prefetching created duplicate 'shadow' entries across KV cache shards, producing a sustained memory amplification and cascading evictions. This ticket captures the remediation work, telemetry improvements, and longer-term design changes to make prefetch and reconciliation idempotent and failover-safe.
impact_summary: During the failover window (2025-02-11 03:18 UTC), multiple nodes rehydrated tenants' KV prefixes concurrently with overlap in prefetch logic. Shadow entries multiplied across shard namespaces leading to a 42% memory spike on the serving cluster, triggered emergency eviction cascades that increased tail latency by ~230ms and caused ~12% 5xx on heavy tenants for 18 minutes.
timeline_summary: 2025-02-11 03:12 - degradations start after cross-region control-plane latency spike; 03:18 - automated failover begins and prefetch storm observed; 03:22 - memory alarms; 03:30 - mitigation rate-limit rolled out to prefetch; 03:50 - memory stabilized after selective tombstone sweep; 04:10 - incremental rollback of the aggressive prefetch heuristic; 2025-02-12 - incident declared and oncall report filed.
root_cause: Simultaneous rehydration from multiple nodes combined with a non-idempotent prefetch/write path created duplicate shadow entries that were not detected by the shard reconciliation logic. The eviction controller used absolute occupancy thresholds without tenant-aware hedging, which amplified eviction score oscillation when shadow entries inflated certain shard's apparent live set.
mitigations_completed: Rolled out emergency prefetch rate-limiter (on/off flag) to reduce new writes during failover window
Executed targeted tombstone sweep on impacted shards to reclaim duplicate shadow entries
Applied temporary eviction-score softening to prevent immediate cascades during stabilization
proposed_fixes: Make prefetch write path idempotent: attach origin-fingerprint and prefetch-epoch to writes and dedupe on apply
Introduce tenant-scoped prefetch quotas that back off automatically during topology changes
Rework shard reconciliation to run a fast de-dup pass for shadow entries during join/rehydration
Change eviction controller to use per-tenant occupancy percentiles and hysteresis windows to avoid score oscillation
Add an async compact-and-merge background job that periodically collapses shadow chains with bounded CPU cost
action_items: (Miguel O) Implement idempotent prefetch write metadata and server-side dedupe check — due 2025-02-28
(Jin L) Add tenant-scoped prefetch budget and fallback behavior in prefetcher — due 2025-03-05
(Priya S) Ship shard reconciliation 'fast de-dupe' algorithm and runbook for rehydration — due 2025-03-03
(SRE Oncall) Create an automated prefetch throttling runbook and alert run (playbook) — due 2025-02-21
(Observability) Implement histogram and cardinality guardrails for prefetched keys per-tenant — due 2025-02-25
(QA) Add chaos tests for cross-region failover with prefetch enabled (see tests_and_validation) — due 2025-03-07
telemetry_requirements: Alert: sudden >20% delta in shard memory used after topology change
Add correlated trace: prefetch.write -> shard.apply -> eviction.score change
tests_and_validation: Unit tests covering idempotent prefetch metadata handling
Integration: rehydration scenario that launches 3 nodes concurrently with overlapping prefetch; assert no duplicate live keys
Load test: synthetic tenant with high prefix cardinality to validate eviction hysteresis prevents cascades
Chaos: simulate region control-plane latency and verify prefetch budget backoff triggers
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout in three phases: 1) server-side dedupe code behind feature flag (canary to 5% traffic), 2) enable tenant prefetch budgets for staging and low-traffic regions, 3) gradually enable global. Each phase runs for 48h with automated rollback on memory or 5xx regressions. Final cutover coordinated with SRE maintenance window.
